We are given $e^{i \alpha} + e^{i \beta} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{7} i.$
We want to find $e^{-i \alpha} + e^{-i \beta}.$
Recall that $e^{-i \theta} = \cos(\theta) - i \sin(\theta)$ for any angle $\theta.$
So, $e^{-i \alpha} + e^{-i \beta} = (\cos(\alpha) - i \sin(\alpha)) + (\cos(\beta) - i \sin(\beta)) = \cos(\alpha) + \cos(\beta) - i (\sin(\alpha) + \sin(\beta)).$

From the given equation, we can see that $\cos(\alpha) + \cos(\beta) = \frac{1}{4}$ and $\sin(\alpha) + \sin(\beta) = \frac{3}{7}.$
Therefore, $e^{-i \alpha} + e^{-i \beta} = \boxed{\frac{1}{4} - \frac{3}{7} i}.$
The answer is: \frac{1}{4}

grade.gold_answer:
We can write
\[\cos \alpha + i \sin \alpha + \cos \beta + i \sin \beta = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{7} i,\]so $\cos \alpha + \cos \beta = \frac{1}{4}$ and $\sin \alpha + \sin \beta = \frac{3}{7}.$  Therefore,
\begin{align*}
e^{-i \alpha} + e^{-i \beta} &= \cos (-\alpha) + i \sin (-\alpha) + \cos (-\beta) + i \sin (-\beta) \\
&= \cos \alpha - i \sin \alpha + \cos \beta - i \sin \beta \\
&= \boxed{\frac{1}{4} - \frac{3}{7} i}.
\end{align*}
